name: 2018 livery
description: White fuselage with a large red 'Austrian' over the forward windows. The fin is the Austrian flag set on a slant: red tip, a broad white band sloping down aft, a red wedge at the root, with the red Austrian arrow on the white. The red runs down onto the rear fuselage and round the tail cone, its forward edge slanting back from the fin's leading edge to the belly. Red wingtips.

sources.note: The 2018 livery, introduced with the rebrand in March 2018.

logos.description: The Austrian arrow (also read as a stylised bird): a long blade from the leading edge slanting down aft, folding back into a short stroke that points down; red on the white band.

titles.style: The Austrian wordmark: a bold, slightly condensed serif with bracketed slab-like serifs, mixed case, upright; set low so the letters cross the window line.

notes: Not drawn: the registration with the Austrian flag and 'Member of Lufthansa Group' small ahead of the red block, a Star Alliance star by the cockpit. On the 787 and 777 the red block's edge follows the fin root further aft. Whether the arrow is mirrored on the right side to point forward isn't confirmed from a right-side photo here. The 2018 scheme replaced the 2003 one (red-white-red tail with the arrow on red, 'Austrian' in gray); by 2026 the fleet is repainted. Re-checked 2026-11-15: the title's lowercase measured at 0.72 of the capitals; the red block's forward edge reduced to its two ends (straight from the side). tools/photo_trace.py couldn't fit the OE-LZC photos (all three are strongly three-quarter views: doors 50 px off), so no edges were moved; by eye on the side-on right-side photo the title's capitals reach about two-thirds of the way to the crown, so its cap height went from 0.44 to 0.6.
